To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) ROI-dependent mechanisms contribute to the decline of the immune function during physio- or premature aging; (ii) imbalanced ROI contribute to driving immunosenesence, chronic inflammation, and autoimmunity; (iii) ROI offer a potential for therapeutic targeting; and (iv) such modifications carry a marked risk for side effects.
reactive oxygen intermediates are involved in the pathogenesis of immunosenescence and chronic inflammatory diseases.
reactive oxygen intermediates are critically involved in the pathomechanisms of immunosenescence and chronic inflammatory diseases.

the identification and analysis of pathomechanisms that are involved in the decline of immune functions during the aging process.
the identification of the molecular and biochemical mechanisms of aging and chronic inflammation.
the elucidation of pathomechanisms of immunosenescence and chronic inflammation in order to develop strategies for their therapeutic targeting.

the ROI-mediated pathomechanisms contributing to immunosenescene, chronic inflammation and autoimmune disease are complex, and their therapeutic targeting is still in its infancy.

ROI-mediated damage is an important contributor to immunosenescenc, chronic inflammation and/or autoimmunity and that the fine tuning of ROI metabolism and signalling is a key factor for a healthy immune function.
the ROI-dependent pathomechanisms contributing to immunosenescene and autoimmunity are highly complex and may be difficult to target in an effective manner.

a better understanding of the complex interplay between ROI and their cellular targets will help to develop more specific and safe therapeutic approaches to prevent and/or treat immunosenescence and age-associated diseases.
